spans.s:
Ula is the name of some unknown wild animal, perhaps, as Whitney suggests, the ‘jackal.’ It is mentioned in the Atharvaveda and later Saṃhitās, but not definitely identified by the commentators.
Foot notes Translation of the Atharvaveda, 669.
xii. 1, 49.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 12, 1 (as ūla); Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 13, 12; 14, 2; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 31. Cf. ulala in baudhāyana śrauta sūtra, ii. 5.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 82.
Ūla is a variant of ula.
Ula vārṣṇi-vṛddha is mentioned as a teacher in the kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa (vii. 4).

Ulapa is the name of a species of grass referred to in the Rigveda and the later Saṃhitās.
Foot notes x. 142, 3.
Av. vii. 66, 1. Adjectives derived from the word are ulapya (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xvi. 45, etc.) and upolapa (Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, i. 7, 2).
